question: If the bot had bought, each month, the companies the fundamental outlook (fundamental_outlook.py, as rebuilt on 2026-11-10) ranks highest by forward earnings yield, would it have made money -- and more than simply holding the same eligible companies, the index, or bills?
researcher: Claude, at the user's request of 2026-11-10 ('check whether trading the stocks the forward-looking section recommends would be profitable')
why_this_is_a_fair_test: The outlook's rules were written on 2026-11-10 from today's cross-section of filings (data errors, statement bases, flag calibration) without looking at any return. No experiment has tested a forward-earnings-yield ranking on any window, so the whole filing history is out of sample for THIS hypothesis. The Codal backfill completed on 2026-11-08 (23,491 filings, 96% of equities), which is what makes a point-in-time test possible at all.

data.filings: codal_filings through backtesting/pit.py: a filing is visible from the first session whose close follows its publication timestamp; undated filings unusable; when an unaudited and an audited release of a period are both public the later one is used. Subsidiary statements were purged on 2026-11-10 and are refused by title.
data.prices: price_history via PointInTimeData.bars(): back-adjusted for capital increases (returns); raw printed close for valuation (valuation_price).
data.shares: capital / 1,000 par from the newest visible filing, scaled by the back-adjustment factor between that filing's period end and the decision date, so a bonus issue after the period end is reflected (the live outlook uses the exchange's share count, which has no history in the database). A dividend gap above the adjustment threshold is misread as a share change by this method -- declared, it lowers the measured yield of large payers.
data.monthly_reports: NOT used: ن-30 history in the store starts in 1405, so every historical estimate uses the statement methods (year_completed / next_year_trend). The live outlook uses monthly reports for ~60% of its ranking; this test therefore measures the statement-based ranking.
data.window: first decision 2021-06-01 (1400/03/11; filings for >=400 companies visible) through 2026-10-31

strategy.decision: every 21 sessions (pit.rebalance_dates), after the close of decision session D
strategy.eligible: equities whose sector is NOT in config.EARNINGS_MULTIPLE_NOT_MEANINGFUL (the outlook's operating-company list), traded on D, 20-session average traded value >= 5e9 rials (500m tomans), newest period <= 7 months old, method not 'annualised', forward earnings yield > 0, not suspect (fundamental_outlook.suspect_reason), at most 1 flag
strategy.hurdle_flag: the bill-yield 'required growth' flag is DISABLED (opportunity rate passed as 0): there is no historical bill-yield series, and inventing one would put an unmeasured number into the selection
strategy.ranking: forward earnings yield, highest first (fundamental_outlook.analyse with rows from pit.fundamental_history(periods=12), today = the Jalali date of D)
strategy.execution: buy and sell at the close of D+1 (the next session). A name locked in a buy queue on D+1 (ExecutionModel.queue_state) cannot be bought and the next-ranked name is taken. A held name that does not trade on the exit session is marked at its last close.
strategy.costs: 1.039% per round trip (backtest_config: 0.464 buy + 0.075 sell + 0.5 tax), charged on the fraction of the book that changes at each rebalance; a name held over is not charged

benchmarks.B1_eligible_ew: equal weight of EVERY eligible company at the same dates, same execution, same costs on its turnover -- the control that isolates the ranking from the market
benchmarks.B2_tedpix: TEDPIX from D+1 close to the next D+1 close
benchmarks.B3_bills: 30% a year, accrued per session -- a round figure between the ~20% deposit rate of 2021 and the ~43% bill yield of 2026; reported, not tested
benchmarks.B4_random_null: 1,000 portfolios of 10 names drawn uniformly from the same eligible, buyable list at every date, same execution. Compared GROSS of costs: a random draw turns the whole book over every period and would be charged costs the ranked book, which keeps names it still ranks, does not pay.

hypotheses.H1: The top-10 portfolio beats the eligible equal-weight portfolio (B1).

test.primary_statistic: mean of per-period log excess returns, top-10 minus B1, net of each one's costs
test.significance: one-sided t-test on the per-period excess returns, Newey-West standard error with 2 lags; alpha 0.05
test.random_null: percentile of the top-10's cumulative GROSS return among the 1,000 random portfolios' cumulative gross returns
test.stability: the excess return computed separately for the first and the second half of the decision dates

decision_rule.ACCEPT: all three: (1) p < 0.05, (2) random-null percentile >= 90, (3) positive mean excess in BOTH halves
decision_rule.REJECT: otherwise. A REJECT is reported as the answer to the user's question: the ranking did not show a selection edge.
decision_rule.no_retuning: N, the cadence, the liquidity floor and the flag limit are fixed here. Results for N=5 and N=20 and for a 63-session cadence are reported as sensitivity and cannot change the decision. If H1 is rejected it is not re-run with other parameters under this ID.

declared_limits: Survivorship: the filings were collected for companies listed today, so companies that delisted in 2021-2026 are absent from both the strategy and B1. The comparison with B1 is the robust one; the absolute returns are flattered.
Monthly reports are not used (see data.monthly_reports).
Shares from capital lines adjusted by price gaps, not the exchange's history (see data.shares).
Fills at the close of D+1 with no market impact beyond the queue rule; a 10-name book of retail size is assumed.
Nominal returns: inflation ran 40-90% over the window, so beating bills or the index is the meaningful comparison, not a positive number.

Dividends: back-adjustment adds back only price gaps above the 12% threshold, so most cash dividends are counted as price falls. This understates the strategy and B1 alike (the comparison between them is unaffected) and favours B2, since TEDPIX includes dividends -- by roughly the market's dividend yield, a few percent a year.
expected_failure: Every stock-selection rule tested in this repository so far (E19-E26) failed to beat random selection. A forward-earnings-yield ranking is a value tilt; in Iran 2021-2026 value tilts have been reported both ways, and the cheapest names are often cheap for reasons the filings show only later. The most likely outcome is a REJECT.
